publish-boundary-test.ref: server/killSwitchSharing.test.ts (13) + server/publishChokePoint.test.ts (13). socialPublish.ts changed in two ways and both are covered. (1) The kill-switch check was EXTRACTED to killSwitchBlockedPlatforms so igAutopost — an autonomous cron measured at 116 live posts in prod — could share the operator's emergency stop instead of bypassing it. killSwitchSharing.test.ts pins the guard's decisions (global / publishing / per-platform, the DENY audit record naming WHICH switch fired, and the deliberate fail-open when switch state is unreadable) AND pins that the extraction left publishToSocial behaviourally identical — including the partial-block case where one platform is stopped and the other still publishes, which is the behaviour most likely to be lost in an extraction. (2) A `link` field was added, because its absence was WHY nickActions.socialPost reached around the door to metaSocial.socialPost; pinned through to postToFacebook. publishChokePoint.test.ts holds the claim gates at contentAdmin.publishCarousel and nickActions.socialPost, and adds a structural sweep asserting no NEW file can import the low-level publishers — the part that makes it stick, since adStudio was fixed alone on 2026-07-25 and this identical defect survived on three other surfaces. Both structural assertions red-green verified: planting a file that imports postToInstagram fails the sweep by name; removing igAutopost's guard branch while keeping the call fails its pin. CADENCE IS NOT CLAIMED — this change deliberately did NOT apply the feed cap to igAutopost, because policy v7 sets maxFeedPostsPerDay=2 while the autoposter has been doing 3/day on 8 of the last 14 active days, and that conflict is the operator's to resolve, not this PR's to decide silently. PR #1127.

cron-fail-closed.ref: server/ros083BriefPriorities.test.ts (9), mutation-verified three ways. The cron file changed here is cron/jobs/morningBrief.ts, and the fail-closed question has an unusual answer for it, so it is worth being precise rather than reciting the pattern.  THIS JOB HAS NO SEND-OR-HOLD DECISION TO GET WRONG. It reads, it composes text, and it calls sendTelegram exactly once at the end — one message, to the owner, with no customer contact anywhere on the path. There is no claim, no queue drain, no per-recipient loop, and nothing to double-send. The failure modes that fail-closed exists to prevent (duplicate customer SMS, a re-fired batch, a half-claimed row) cannot occur here.  WHAT COULD GO WRONG INSTEAD is the brief being WRONG rather than absent, and that is the direction this change moves. Nothing new can throw: buildDecisionsBlock is pure and total — every branch returns a string, there is no path through it that can reject — and it is called inside the SAME try/catch that already wrapped the topDecisions read. The catch still logs and still continues; what changed is that it now assigns an explicit UNAVAILABLE line instead of leaving "". So the job's success/failure surface to the scheduler is byte-for-byte what it was: sendMorningBrief still returns { recordsProcessed: 1, details } on the happy path, still returns { details: 'DB unavailable' } when the top-level db() handle is null, and still throws only from the reads that could already throw.  The one behavioural change on the failure path is that the brief now SAYS the priority queue could not be read. That is strictly more conservative than before: previously the LLM filled the mandated 'Top 3 priorities' section from whatever else was in the data blob and the operator received invented priorities formatted as queue-backed ones.  topDecisions gained `queryable: boolean`, which is additive. Checked rather than assumed: shared/bridgeShapes.ts TopDecisionsShape is a non-strict z.object, so the other consumer (routes/nour-os-query.ts, which hands the result to the Telegram bridge) keeps parsing unchanged, and server/__tests__/bridge-shapes.test.ts stays green — including its drift case, which asserts a fixture MISSING totalLive is rejected.  Mutations verified RED and each file restored byte-identical: letting the unqueryable case fall through turns 1 case red, returning "" on a genuinely empty queue turns 2 red, deleting the prompt rule turns 1 red. NOT CLAIMED: no live cron tick, no LLM call, no Telegram message — the scheduler-surface claims above are read from cron/scheduler.ts and cron/index.ts, not measured against a deployed run.

operator-walkthrough.ref: WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES, on a phone — /admin -> Instagram -> Action Center, a new card at the top: "Bring in a finished MP4". Collapsed by default (Action Center's job is to surface what is STUCK, not to lead with a form). Open it and there are three fields — file path or public URL, topic, caption — and one button that reads "Ingest as draft", which on the first tap becomes "Tap again to ingest".  BEFORE: there was nothing. ingestFinishedMp4 shipped with twelve passing tests and ZERO importers — grep found it referenced only by its own spec. The flag was registered in the env-gates panel, so an operator reading that panel would conclude the feature existed and was merely switched off. Arming MP4_INGEST_ENABLED would have done nothing at all, because no code path reached the function.  The card says, in the description under the title, that the file lands as a review-ready DRAFT, that it does NOT publish, and that it still passes every approval and publish gate. That copy is load-bearing: "ingest" reads like "publish" if nothing tells you otherwise, and this button now sits on the same screen as the publish actions. A second line under the path field says the URL must be permanent, because a presigned link works right up until the publish gate fetches it hours later when the operator is no longer watching — the service refuses those up front and this says so before the tap rather than after.  The confirm is two-tap and in DOM. window.confirm is silently suppressed in the operator's standalone iOS PWA, so a confirm() gate here would be no gate at all; lint:source enforces the absence of the global and a test asserts something took its place. Server errors are surfaced VERBATIM in the toast — each one names something actionable (the flag is off · that is not an mp4 · that URL expires) and "ingest failed" would hide all three.  ★ THE TESTS ASSERT THE WIRING, NOT THE SERVICE, and that distinction is the whole point. A unit test of ingestFinishedMp4 could never have caught this defect: the service was already fully tested and still unreachable. server/mp4IngestDoor.test.ts (10) asserts that a router exposes it, that the route is an admin MUTATION rather than a query or a public procedure, that a client surface actually calls that route, that the two-tap arm exists, and that the router does NOT duplicate the service's own ftyp / presigned / flag checks — a second copy of a rule is a second place for it to drift.  It is on contentAdmin beside listInventory and actOnInventoryItem, because what it produces is an inventory row those two already manage. NOT on socialPipeline, which registers the flag but declares itself READ-ONLY in its own header ("It never writes, posts, or mutates").  EVIDENCE: server/mp4IngestDoor.test.ts (10), MUTATION-VERIFIED THREE WAYS — removing the router procedure turns 4 cases red, removing the client caller turns 1 red, removing the two-tap arm turns 1 red; both files restored byte-identical (0 residual markers). Full serial suite green: 392 files passed / 2 skipped, 4,845 passed / 50 skipped / 1 todo, exit 0. tsc --noEmit clean, lint:source clean (client dialog globals: 0).  NOT CLAIMED, and recorded as the still-open P2 on the mp4-ingest capability: NOTHING HAS BEEN INGESTED END TO END, in any environment. The flag has never been armed, no mp4 has passed the ftyp check against a real file, and no ingested draft has reached the publish gate. Reachable is not proven — the ledger entry stays at unit_verified. NOTE ON THIS KEY: last-writer-wins by design; the manifest lives on main while requirements are derived per-diff.

capability-ledger-updated.deferred: No capability gains or loses a state, so no ledger entry is edited. The rule fires on one changed file under server/services/**: opportunityQueue.ts. That change is one additive field on topDecisions' return — `queryable: boolean`, false when the queue could not be CONSULTED at all (no database handle, or revenue_opportunities missing because migration 0099 is unapplied). Both of those cases already returned an empty result and still do; the field only lets a caller tell them apart from 'asked, and there is genuinely nothing to do'. No query changed, no ranking changed, no row is written, no new surface is exposed, and the populated path is byte-for-byte identical — a test asserts the listed block still renders decisions verbatim with value, evidence and attempts, and still prints 'value unknown' rather than $0. Nothing nickstire CAN DO changed. The operator-facing change is that the morning brief now admits when the priority queue was unreadable instead of letting the model invent priorities — a truthfulness fix to an existing output, not a capability. Checked rather than assumed: there is NO ledger entry for the revenue-opportunity queue or for the morning brief. The nearest by name is `shadow-planner` (Shadow-mode opportunity planner, integration_verified), and it is not the right home — it describes the planner that PROPOSES opportunities, not the read path that surfaces them in the brief, and its state is unaffected by an additive boolean on a consumer-side query. This PR also deliberately does not CREATE an entry for the queue. Registering a capability is a claim about what the system does, and the honest state for revenue_opportunities depends on whether migration 0099 is applied in production — which this change neither applies nor verifies. Minting an entry on the strength of a unit-tested boolean is exactly the unearned claim this ledger exists to prevent. EVIDENCE for the behaviour change lives on the operator-walkthrough entry: server/ros083BriefPriorities.test.ts (9), mutation-verified three ways, plus server/__tests__/bridge-shapes.test.ts staying green to show the additive field did not drift the bridge contract.

render-spend-trajectory.ref: server/reelRepairLaneTruth.test.ts (12) + server/selectiveRepair.test.ts (8), mutation-verified three ways.  WHAT THE SPEND ACTUALLY DID BEFORE. selectiveRepair hardcoded provider:"higgsfield", model:"seedance1_5", COST_ESTIMATES_USD.seedance_clip and a direct import of higgsfieldStudio — on a path that runs for EVERY reel regardless of which provider generated it. Two consequences, and the second is the expensive one. (1) The ledger lied: a repair on a Veo job was filed as Higgsfield/seedance1_5 at the Seedance price, so every provider-comparison figure and the daily budget both counted the wrong number, and a repair on a template_stock job — which costs nothing — consumed real budget and could push maxGenerationCostPerDayUsd over for renders that are free. (2) It actually CALLED Higgsfield: a shop pinned to the free local lane got a real paid API render the moment any beat needed repair. The provider pin is a deliberate cost decision and the repair path was quietly overriding it in the paid direction.  AFTER: repair calls selectReelVideoProvider(), reserves and settles the SAME reelClipCostUsd(provider) figure, records reelLedgerModel(provider) from the one shared map the generation path already uses, routes template_stock to local ffmpeg (free, and it stays local), and REFUSES a provider it has no branch for by name rather than falling through to one that costs money. That refusal mirrors the generation path's own precedent — reelPipeline already throws on an unhandled REEL_VIDEO_PROVIDER rather than letting it reach the Veo branch.  THE ENQUEUE GATE WAS WRONG IN THE OTHER DIRECTION and is fixed in the same change: enforceAtBoundary was handed COST_ESTIMATES_USD.seedance_clip, so the policy gate could REFUSE a template_stock repair — one that costs nothing — on the grounds of a budget it would never touch. It is now priced at the active lane. A gate is only as good as the number it is handed.  ★ THE EXISTING SUITE WENT RED, AND THAT IS THE FINDING RATHER THAN A CHORE. Two cases in server/selectiveRepair.test.ts assert on the prompt handed to generateReelClipVideo — they exercise the Higgsfield path — but they never SAID so, because the code hardcoded it and there was nothing to say. The moment the code started asking which lane it was on, those tests were revealed to have no opinion: with no REEL_VIDEO_PROVIDER set they were silently running whatever auto-select picks. A suite with no opinion about the provider cannot notice a repair rendering on the wrong one, which is exactly how this survived. They now pin REEL_VIDEO_PROVIDER=higgsfield explicitly, unstubbed in afterEach because this suite runs single-fork on Windows and a leaked env var follows into other files.  LEDGER: the template-stock-reel-lane deferredScope item that registered this defect is rewritten rather than deleted, and it CORRECTS ITS OWN CLAIM about visualWorld.ts. That file was named alongside selectiveRepair as the same bug; it is not. visualWorld generates reference IMAGES through generateCarouselSlideImage at the gpt_image_2 rate, REEL_VIDEO_PROVIDER selects a VIDEO provider, and template_stock has no image generator at all — so its provider:"higgsfield" label is ACCURATE today. It is deliberately left alone, with a note that it acquires this same defect the day an image-provider lane exists. Also recorded as still true: ESTIMATED_REEL_RENDER_COST_USD at the reel enqueue boundary remains a flat per-reel constant and is still not provider-aware.  MUTATIONS, each verified RED with the file restored byte-identical: re-hardcoding provider+model in the reservation turns 1 case red · deleting the refusal so an unbranched provider falls through to Higgsfield turns 2 red · returning the policy gate to the flat Seedance constant turns 1 red. Full serial suite green: 391 files passed / 2 skipped, 4,838 passed / 50 skipped / 1 todo, exit 0. tsc --noEmit clean.  NOT CLAIMED: no live spend trajectory and no production repair. Nothing here was measured against generation_reservations in prod — the assertions are on which figure and which provider the code reserves, settles and gates with, not on money observed moving.
